- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to undercorrect — forecast is too low, especially in early days of the 30d horizon.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3), model often overestimates, especially after recent spikes — forecast overshoots true price.  
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of the 30d forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 18d mean), model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged upward trend — true price often corrects faster.  
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds onto momentum longer than observed in true price, especially when sentiment is mixed or negative.  
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust downward quickly — true price often drops faster than forecast.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging the true price by 2–5 days — especially when sentiment is volatile or trending.  
- Model ignores sentiment decay — if sentiment drops sharply, forecast doesn’t adjust until later, leading to persistent underestimation.
